config_name: Surface Pro 11 — Snapdragon X Plus (Lumen, 10-core), 16GB, 256GB, 13" LCD touch + Signature Keyboard

specs.cpu: Qualcomm Snapdragon X Plus X1P-42-100 "Lumen" (10-core Oryon, 3.4GHz)
specs.display_type: PixelSense Flow LCD IPS glossy touch, 3:2
specs.keyboard_notes: Signature Keyboard included in entry price (sold separately by MS); backlit chiclet, small trackpad
specs.pen_support: Surface Slim Pen 2 supported, sold separately (~CA$159.99)

battery.notes: 48Wh. LCD panel + lower-bin X Plus = best endurance of the line. CNET measured just under 13h video on OLED X Elite; LCD X Plus typically a bit better.

price.notes: Tablet-only est CA$1,399.99 (CA launch MSRP; microsoft.com/en-ca unfetchable at research time) + Signature Keyboard est CA$199.99. Keyboard sold separately — price INCLUDES it per site rule. 512GB twin verified at BBY for CA$1,499.99 sale.

reviews.quote: the Surface Pro 11's Qualcomm Snapdragon X Elite finally breaks the mold, delivering surprisingly competitive performance and a lot fewer compatibility issues for mainstream use

professional.notes: CNET did not test X Plus explicitly ('I haven't tested the lower-power Snapdragon X Plus'). Ratings inferred from X Elite OLED anchor; see SHARED-surface-pro.md.

praises: Battery routinely hits a full workday-plus; LCD + X Plus is the endurance pick of the line (BBY 4.63★/99 on the 512GB twin)
Silent fanless operation — zero noise in office use
Performance on battery stays near plugged-in levels, unlike x86 convertibles (CNET)
Kickstand with 155° range and tablet form factor loved for couch/pen use
Windows Hello face unlock is instant even in the dark (IR camera)
complaints: Keyboard sold separately — real laptop price is ~CA$200+ above sticker
LCD tier is 60Hz and dull next to the OLED sibling; glossy glass reflects everything
No 3.5mm headphone jack on any Pro 11
ARM app gaps: some peripherals, plugins and anti-cheat games still don't run
16GB shared with GPU fills up fast under many browser tabs (CNET: '16GB is not enough')

design_philosophy: Microsoft's flagship detachable tablet: fanless ARM silicon for all-day silence and battery, a 3:2 touch/kickstand design that doubles as a pen tablet, with Windows-on-ARM finally reaching mainstream app compatibility. This X Plus LCD tier is the affordable Copilot+ entry — same chassis and NPU as the OLED models, trading display polish and GPU bin for price and endurance.
rating_notes: Ratings inferred from CNET 8.3 review of the X Elite 16/1TB OLED config (SHARED-surface-pro.md): LCD 60Hz sRGB vs OLED → screen_quality −2.3, readability_dark −1.5; X Plus lower GPU bin → gaming −0.7, productivity −1.0; LCD + lower TDP → battery +0.5; Signature Keyboard (no pen storage, thinner) → keyboard_trackpad −1.0 vs Flex Keyboard tiers. Replaceable SSD under kickstand lifts upgradability vs fully-soldered rivals.
